utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you, Admiral, of the affirmation. Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I start off by asking for the usher's assistance to distribute a document and hand one copy to the witness. Your Honour, I have to say at the outset that this document has not been translated into B/C/S. We were disclosed the document by the Prosecution during the cross-examination, so we were not able to have it translated, and I'll just briefly be asking a few questions and introduce it by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean to say it had not been translated into English?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I misspoke. I said B/C/S, but what I meant was English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that's the one mistake you're allowed today, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, is this document familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a regular combat report from my command. It is dated the 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take this document from the military archives?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I didn't take anything from the archives. You cannot take anything out of archives, so I wasn't able to take a single piece of paper out of the archives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you received a copy of this document, did you not, from the military archives?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I think that the Defence counsel might have been given copies, but I haven't see it. But I did see it in the archives, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the signatory is the chief of staff, captain of the battleship, Milan Zec; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's a regular combat report of the command of the 9th VPS. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, under point 1, what do we have there? What's this about? Could you make things a bit clearer, because as I said, we don't have the document in English, so I should like to ask you to explain it to us.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In point 1, it is stated that the enemy went into the following action: From 1330 to 1515 hours, from the position -- from a position 150 metres left of the Libertas Hotel, from Srdj and Nuncijata and Lokrum, 82-millimetre mortars were used, and 100-millimetre ones. And our positions at Dubac were fired at, Zarkovica, Brgat. Dubac, Zarkovica, and Brgat were targeted. 80 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says 50 here.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately 50 fell on Dubac, about 60 on Brgat, and at Zarkovica, an unascertained number of mines. The enemy recorded our positions exactly because the mines fell to within 5 metres of our front line, front flank. At the same time from the positions at Bosanka, machine-gun fire was opened at the Zarkovica position, and rifle fire as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, the facts contained in point 1 of this regular combat report dated the 6th of November 1991, do they correspond to the facts and figures that we read out and saw yesterday in document D54, which you recognised by its style, the style in which it was written and you said that yes, quite possibly it was compiled by your assistant for political affairs. First of all, with respect to the figures, the numbers of shells falling on JNA positions and the positions from which the JNA was targeted.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they do correspond in part, but I must say why I reacted yesterday when it came to the number of shells that were listed, and I'm going to be, as I always am, very frank and open and honest. Under my level of professional soldier -- or when I read that the assistant for political affairs in my command --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you speed up a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, when he says that 61 shells fell on one position and 63 or 53 - I can't remember the exact number - shells, and on the 3rd, 100 or 200 shells, it is not possible to ascertain this exactly. So it's a little suspect, or rather, I did not accept this piece of information readily. However, we see here the exact figures as they would be compiled by a professional, objectively acceptable facts and figures. It says, "approximately 50," "approximately 60," and so on and so forth. So that is the professional attitude, and that is my explanation along with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the difference is in those precise figures.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to ask you to look at point 2 of this same document and to tell us what point 2 is about. Once again, it refers to JNA units, a description of JNA unit activities.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that our units from the position -- from their positions targeted Bosanka, the sports hall, and Hotel -- the sports hall, Hotel Libertas, Srdj, and Bosanka with cannons and from tanks. And Srdj and Bosanka were targeted with a cannon of 130 millimetres and 122-millimetre cannons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This 122 millimetres, is that 12 shells of a 122-millimetre Howitzer?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says 12 HA 122 millimetres. Would that be Howitzers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have the figures, the digits, "1 times 130 MX," and then "12 HA 122 MM." So what would that be?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the deployment, or rather the unit at Srdj and several houses in Bosanka from which they opened fire. On our side, there were no casualties. We mined the area and placed obstacles on approaches to the Trapit hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did the JNA units open fire only after there was fire, as described -- extensive fire and targeting of their positions as described in point 1?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. From this, we can see that on our side we opened fire only after we had been fired on and targeted by the enemy side, after 1515 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this legitimate action on the part of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have the usher's assistance again, please, and could he please hand D49, Defence Exhibit D49, to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, we've already seen this document. It is your order for the deployment of the artillery issued on the 6th of November, once again, at 9.00 in the morning. It says "urgent," and it was sent to the 472nd Brigade. This is -- rather, we now have this regular combat report as well in front of us. Tell me, please, are there any contradictions between these two documents? How is it possible that you forbid something, whereas the army Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. goes into action, into operation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. You mean how -- I'm forbidding something here, and yet the army is going into operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you forbid the use of the artillery because of the negotiations underway with the EC mission.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you issued this order at 9.00 in the morning, and you marked it urgent. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, looking through this regular combat report which was signed by the chief of staff Zec, that the action your units went into are described under point 2, they are completely legitimate and lawful?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you explain that to us, please. How can that be possible?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here, what is stated is the following: This order does not exclude the obligation of the units and command of the 472nd Brigade to suggest the use of artillery if they evaluate it as necessary. And in the combat report issued on the same day at 1700 hours, we can see that operations from the opposite side, from the enemy side, by using artillery between 1300 hours and 1500 hours targeting the Dubac, Zarkovica, and Brgat area was so strong that we needed to react.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your command, did it give the okay to go into action and react?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this report, we can also see that the artillery battalion didn't go into action, the 130-millimetre ones or the 122-millimetre batteries. All that happened was an order that was issued for two cannons to go into action. And I can't read the third one. It's probably a 120-millimetre mortar. But at all events, there were two or three artillery pieces which were intended for precision targeting of point-like or dot-like targets with the aim of neutralising fire at one location, at one position, and not as support to a unit engaged in an attack or to go into operation in a broader area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, under item 2 of the regular combat report, it says that your units opened fire against the following: Srdj, Bosanka, and the sports hall near the Libertas Hotel with cannons from tanks while Srdj and Bosanka, with 1 times 130 millimetres and 12 HA. That is -- that designates a Howitzer, and it's 122 millimetres. So it is not one objective; it is several objectives or targets.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was two cannons, not two targets. I said it was two cannons that were supposed to fire. These are very precise cannons from the technical experimental centre. It is not a tactical unit. That was my point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell me, is HA a Howitzer? A 122-millimetre Howitzer?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Instead of that number 2, it's probably supposed to say 1 times HA 122 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it perhaps 12 shells from a Howitzer of 122 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so because there is no number of shells, how many shells were fired from the 130-millimetre piece. So probably it's just a mistake, a typo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, a Howitzer is not an artillery piece that is intended to engage point objectives or targets.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not? Why not? A Howitzer of 105 millimetres and 150 millimetres are real Howitzers, whereas this is the so-called Gvozdika Howitzer of 122 millimetres, so it's not a classical Howitzer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In accordance with your morning report of the 6th of November, artillery could only be used on orders coming from the command post and the forward command post of the 9th VPS. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But that was for the 472nd Brigade. It was addressed to it specifically, and this report does not refer to that brigade. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which unit does this report speak of?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that there are two cannons. It is well known where these two cannons were. These are only two cannons. A brigade cannot use two cannons only for firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can a battalion, a company?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they cannot. A brigade and a battalion did not have 130-millimetre cannons or Howitzers. It's only a command brigade that has this, and also an artillery battalion, and that is 10 to 15 kilometres from the area where it is used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit was then engaged in this shooting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said already that these were two cannons of the technical experimental centre under the command of the sector 130-millimetre battery. That is the chief of staff Zec. He had it under his direct command. It was used rarely, only for engaging point targets where it is necessary to have very precise targeting, without any deviation or error. These cannons were used only a few times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about when Srdj was targeted? Was there a danger of hitting the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not with these cannons, no. Only if a battery that has that large margin of error in the ellipsis, or if there are misses as such, then it is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could this cannon also miss a target?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cannon could miss a target, but it doesn't have an ellipsis; it is one shell. So that's why I said that with this, that it's not a reservist or some squad leader who used this cannon for targeting. It was done by a specialist from the technical experimental centre, and he only used that cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he could not miss. That's what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this cannon did not have any shell dispersion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any one can, but his was minimal, perhaps up to 20 metres, 30 metres. But not a hundred metres or 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But since you say that this was directly under the control of your chief of staff Zec --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- he was not afraid that due to the targeting of Srdj and the sports hall near Libertas there could be mistakes, errors, that the shells would fall too far away or too close?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he certainly had no such fear. That is why he took these cannons, as I said, and these two specialists who were trained to such an extent that they certainly could not have had any misses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me the names of these two specialists?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They are civilians. They did have one noncommissioned officer there. I remember that. But they had two civilians, too, I think, who belonged to the Military Technical Institute, and their task, even in training, was to maintain with maximum precision these cannons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the guns from the tanks that you refer to that opened fire?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Zarkovica, in the area of Zarkovica, we had two tanks - I think they had been brought there by then - that were within the 3rd Battalion because the battery -- or rather, the tank company that the tactical group, the 2nd Tactical Group had was disbanded, this company was, and only four tanks remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these tanks of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, they were not within the battalion because this battalion had not been brought in as such. It was on leave. However, they were at Zarkovica then for defence. They were dug in for defence of the area of Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under whose command were these tanks?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the unit that was there, the 4th Battalion was there then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the 472nd Motorised Brigade? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It was there then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these old tanks, the old type of tanks?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, T-32.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How precise are their guns in terms of targeting anything in town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are guns, cannons, that have a particular trajectory. They can only target the targets they see. They cannot target anything they cannot see. They are precise for 3 to 4 kilometre distances, although the tanks -- so if the tanks themselves are in a very bad condition, the cannons could nevertheless take any objective. They could fire straight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these tanks from the Second World War?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, T-32s are, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of how old these tanks and guns were, how could the chief of staff allow to have targets engaged in town by such weaponry?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No engaging of targets in town is referred to here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the Libertas Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Hotel Libertas is by the sea. Well, in all fairness, yes, it's a part of town, but it's a very protruding building, and there was an 85-millimetre cannon near that hotel, and it was targeting our positions all the time. It was right by the sea, 100 or 200 metres away. That is absolutely at a distance from the settled area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there no risk of this tank missing that particular target by the Libertas Hotel and hitting, say, a civilian building?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a risk. There's always a risk. I agree. However, I say that these are not mortars or cannons that shoot from a long-range, 10 or 15 kilometres. For example, from Zarkovica, they look through binoculars and if they were targeting one particular gun, they can see exactly through binoculars where they had hit. This is not battery gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I would like to have this document tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is marked D55.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to help distribute the following document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document, Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. This is a regular combat report. I see. It pertains to the 8th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the superior command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The IKM, that is to say, the forward command post of the command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in addition to the 2nd Operational Group, it is also sent to the forward command post of the command of the Military Naval District. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We sent documents to them so that they would keep abreast of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you regularly report to the command of the Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you submit these regular combat reports to them, all of them, and the orders you issued?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only combat reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about combat orders?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me why you sent this to the command of the Military Naval District?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said at least once. In order to keep my command abreast of all developments in the units of the 9th VPS, because my command in terms of establishment was and would certainly return to the command of the Military Naval District. And it once again would become subordinate to it. So it would not be all right if combat reports, regular reports, were not sent to that command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody order that kind of thing, to have it sent to the command of the 9th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, interpreter's mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the Military Naval District?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that was the order, but it was the practice, the everyday practice that all reports that were sent to the superior command, the command of the 2nd Operational Group, that also they be sent to the Island of Vis to the forward command post there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who established this practice?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably Admiral Kandic and the previous commander of the 9th Sector because that can be seen there. It dates back all the way to the 1st of October and even before that, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it strange that you report to two superior commands?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no two superior commands. I never said that, either. There is only one superior command, and that is the command of the 2nd Operational Group. That is my command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have approval from the command of the 2nd Operational Group to send regular combat reports along parallel lines, not only to them but also to the command of the Military Naval District?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that that approval is required. And I don't know if my predecessor had it, General Ruzinovski. I don't know. But I think that it is absolutely a particular practice that had no effect whatsoever over the performance of combat duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when you were in -- the commander of the 9th VPS from 1983 to 1989, who was your superior commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Military Naval District.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1991, when you came to the 9th VPS, who was your superior officer?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you receive orders from, or rather orders and other command documents?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the commander of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you send combat reports and information to two addresses rather than one; and in this way, did you jeopardise the elementary principle of military command, and that is the principle of singleness of command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This principle of singleness of command was not jeopardised in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the practice of vertical communication from you, as commander of the 9th VPS, to two commands that are formally at the same level, the Military Naval District and the 2nd Operational Group? Was that one of the hindrances in the effectiveness of command in your particular command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a hinderance of any kind. You cannot even understand this. The combat orders I got from my superior command were not sent to the command of the VPO of the Military Naval District. That would be jeopardising the rules. This simply meant keeping them abreast of what was going on. My -- keeping my former command abreast of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's not waste any time over this. You've already given me an answer. Let's go on. In the regular combat report, under point 1, enemy, it says that on the 8th of November -- rather, the 8th of November, one is enemy; two, the activities of our units. Now, do you describe there an attack that had taken place on the village of Bosanka and that members of your units were wounded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, an attack on Bosanka had been ordered, and in the fighting, eight JNA soldiers were wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which units took part in that attack?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those units were a mixed detachment of the Territorial Defence which was established on the 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the mixed detachment of the Territorial Defence that you yourself established?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, within the frameworks of that mixed TO detachment, was there a unit of Territorial Defence from Herceg-Novi, for instance?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There was a platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, were there any casualties from that unit of the Territorial Defence of Herceg-Novi, I mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. Two dead and two wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did it take two or three days for the dead and wounded members of that unit to be pulled out from those positions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did it take such a long time to pull the dead and wounded out from the area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the ridge, the Dubrava Greben between Bosanka and Srdj is a completely bare area, no trees growing there, no vegetation, just rock. And from town, and from Srdj, you could see anybody moving around, any soldier moving around the area. So we tried, we did our best, to contact the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik and to request that they allow a Red Cross ambulance to go in and pull out the dead and wounded. However, we did not succeed in doing that, in having that agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do then amidst the fighting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For two days we tried by using volunteers. We tried to pull the dead and wounded out with the help of volunteers. There was a great deal of pressure coming from Herceg-Novi itself. And finally, I sent the chief of staff to see General Strugar to prevail upon him to give us one or two APCs because we weren't able to do what we intended even with tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you unable to do this for such a long period of time because the enemy side was targeting you all the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that was the most important reason, the basic reason. There was so much heavy firing, and two more soldiers were killed and three more wounded from all the firing at us. So we ended up having more casualties pulling these out than we did in the combat itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had to pull out the dead and wounded, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as a result of all this, was there dissatisfaction among the members of that territorial Herceg-Novi detachment -- company?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Up until then in the fighting it was usually the Montenegrins who were killed outside the Bay of Boka. This was the first time there were casualties from Herceg-Novi and Boka, and one or two dead from Kotor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there some very well-known sportsmen among the casualties?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The commander of the platoon himself was one. His name was Vojica Pejovic, and there was another sportsman from one of the sports clubs, the Zvezda sports club. I've forgotten his name now. He was a volunteer from Herceg-Novi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, after that, were there protest in front of the headquarters at Kumbor staged by members of that unit and civilians from the town of Herceg-Novi?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There was a protest rally. It was the result both of what had happened and this general dissatisfaction because of the casualties, and also because I prevented the attack on Srdj. I did not wish to allow an attack on Srdj to go forward by any means. But also, that attack was inspired by the letter that we read out here yesterday from Mr. Vucurevic, because people get to hear about it in the units. The soldiers hear about all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are your conclusions, because in Mr. Vucurevic's letter there's not a single word about this situation at Bosanka. Now, I'm going to ask you about another protest staged in front of your headquarters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, you've then just given your interpretation of things. If you want that to be posed as a question to see whether that is the view of the witness, you can. But otherwise, your summary is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in front of your headquarters, in front of the command during those days, were protests staged by the reservists as well who had returned from the Lora port, military port or wartime port in Split?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it wasn't during those days. It was in October, the month of October. And they did not succeed in staging protests in front of the headquarters because I had ordered that they line up and that the police confiscate their weapons as soon as they left the vessel, left the ship. But what they wanted to do was to stage protests in front of the headquarters, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me this, please: In this regular combat report, it is stated that in the fighting around the village of Bosanka, a wounded ZNG member was captured. He was given medical attention and examined and questioned, and he informed the 9th VPS that in the village of Bosanka there were 74 members of the ZNG, the Croatian National Guards Corps, and that he himself had come on a ship upon which Stjepen Mesic, the president of the Yugoslav state Presidency, had sailed with him. Is that the soldier you told us about here in Court? His name was Damir Kos, unless I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That is the soldier, Damir Kos, the one we spoke about. Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, now, because of this operation and action and the casualties was the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade introduced because of that? Was it launched into the fighting in the further operations because of that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was from the aspects of the 2nd Operational Group. And I accepted that, although that was not the demand I had made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your viewpoint, did you feel that those units of the Territorial Defence should have continued to have casualties of that kind and not to accomplish their goals and targets? Is that what should have been continued?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This unit suffered losses without any reason and through the error of its commander. Its commander was to blame. The Bosanka fortress had been taken control of without a single soldier being killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, what I'm asking you is this, and it is something you yourself said: That you were not able to pull your dead and wounded out, and that you had to go to the command of the 2nd Operational Group for assistance, to help you out. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when those killed and wounded were being pulled out, some more soldiers were killed and wounded in the process. So were these considerable losses?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are losses. But I'm saying that Srdj was attacked counter to my orders, and that is why these casualties and losses came about. They were completely unnecessary, without any military or tactical need.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who ordered the attack on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody ordered the attack on Srdj. That's what I'm saying. The platoon commander, instead of setting up an ambush, which is what it said in the order to him, instead of that, he started to attack Srdj, to make himself famous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do with that platoon commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That platoon commander was killed. He's the one we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, fine.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pejovic is his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was undertaken to prevent anything like that happening in future?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the unit was pulled out from combat. It was a platoon, actually, a special platoon, that was what it was referred to, from a Herceg-Novi company. And the steps that were taken are these: Until the very end, I didn't allow Srdj to be taken control of, the facility at Srdj. And if there is occasion, I should be happy to explain this. Despite the order from the 2nd Operational Group, I did not allow that facility at Srdj to be taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, during this period of time, your chief of staff was very active, was he not, in the field, in the area where the units of the 9th VPS were deployed? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes, it is. Those are the orders he was given. He was at the ridge with Colonel Kovacevic. And he was in charge of carrying out those tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to tender this exhibit into evidence. May it be given a number, please, as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit will be D56.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have the usher's assistance, please, in distributing the next document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your order for attack dated the 9th of November 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's some -- the document starts off with some handwriting, and then the typed out text is identical to that. This order for attack was addressed to the 472nd Brigade, the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, and the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, the mixed TO detachment, and the 16th Border Naval Detachment. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, because I haven't seen this document for a long time, so I have to look through it. But I assume what you say is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, under point 1, you are describing the situation linked to the enemy, the enemy positions.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it state here under point 1, referring to the enemy, that the fortress of the Old Town centre is being -- is using mobile MB 82-millimetre mortars and 60-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that how it was? Is that what actually happened, Mr. Jokic? Now we have your order for attack. That's it. So you stand behind it. It doesn't say Zec or anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stand behind this order. But I can't stand behind every nonsensical thing. I didn't think all this was nonsense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this true?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the truth has been imprecisely stated. If you want to hear the real truth, the 82- and 60-millimetre mortars cannot target from the fortress. There is no theoretical possibility of that being possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why did you write that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't write that. It says from the shelter of the fortress. But a mortar has to be on firm ground. It cannot stand on stone. It has to be placed on a platform. But, yes, it says on the fortress or from the shelter of the fortress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they in the shelter of the fortress?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but as I say --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The mortars attacked your units, did they not?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It was an interrupted answer, and it would be good if the witness could finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to conclude that, Admiral?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In order to be more precise, from the shelter, the fort in the Old Town was being used, as it is stated here, by the enemy. This doesn't necessarily mean that they were firing on that same day, but the fort was being used to shelter the mortars they were using. That would be more precise reading of the document, if that's our intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it you just told us, Mr. Jokic? What are these mortars doing in relation to the forts inside the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were using the turrets as shelter in the Old Town. And from those sheltered positions, they were able to fire on our targets, on our units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 1, you say "enemy." Was the enemy, too, in a position to fire, to target you from there, your units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The enemy is firing by 82- and 60-millimetre mortars from the forts inside the Old Town centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is stated here is that they are using mobile mortar units.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mortars as a rule are always mobile. They are not stationary weapons. Well, yes, firing; what else should they be doing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are firing on your units; isn't that right? Or are they perhaps firing into the sea?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we would probably do well to stay serious. Of course they were firing on my units, but not every single thing is stated here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why are you not saying it? I'm asking you for the third time in a row now. That is the only thing you're supposed to say. Enemy mortars firing on your units.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm telling you is that it's not stated literally here but that is understood, it's implicit in the text. They're not just there for purposes of a military parade

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why are you not stating that? You are telling your units about the positions of the enemy, aren't you, under point 1?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I'm just reading the same thing that you've just read out, and this is what it says. Now that you're asking me, I'm telling you exactly what you want to hear. You're asking me, what were they doing there? Well, they were firing. But I'm only reading what it says here, what is written. It is not stated here that they are firing; they are using shelters, from which they were probably firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The objective of the 9th VPS, the task of the 9th VPS, according to this report, was to complete a total blockade of Dubrovnik from both sea and land and force the enemy to surrender. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I received as a task from the commander of the 2nd Operational Group is stated here accurately in this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 4, you state what your decision was. You describe what your decision was, to introduce the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade into the combat disposition of the battalion, of the Trebinje Brigade, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your decision under point 4, is it not stated that those units should break out of the line, Zarkovica, Srdj, Strincjera, Gradci, Komolac, Rijeka Dubrovacka, and establish full blockade of Dubrovnik from land and sea and force the enemy to surrender?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Srdj was included in the definition of this line that your units should have reached?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an order given by the command of the 2nd Operational Group. The line is defined on the ground when you look at the features, at the facilities providing the specific positions of that line. But in my order it is never stated that the facility of Srdj should be taken. I simply did not allow Srdj to be taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how can you reach a line including also Srdj without taking the facility itself?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course, you can. It can be 500 metres in front or behind the feature itself. It doesn't mean that every single facility, every single feature along the line must be taken. If you write that down - and you have failed to provide us with a document of the 2nd Operational Group, we don't know what that one says - take the fort of Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the order of the command of the 2nd Operational Group for this day and for the following day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you have that order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably somewhere in the files.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why didn't you simply bring the document if that's indeed what it says?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not take that document or any other document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the documents that you handed over to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the ones that I was given, but I did not take anything myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, is it your submission that you and your Defence team did not receive the copies of documents you required from the Belgrade military archives?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I told you is that we requested 700 documents and were only given 60.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard that explanation before. But all I'm asking you now is whether you obtained from the military archive copies of those documents, regardless of whether it was just one document or 50 of them.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We requested about 700, but the ones we could actually use amounted to less than 30. These were not handed over to me personally, but rather to my Defence team, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the ones you were actually given -- the one that's somehow missing is precisely this command of this 2nd Operational Group. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that we did not receive even a poor copy. It's simply not even there in relation to the 10th, 11th, or 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is it that it's missing; in the files?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it must be in the files. It's just that we weren't given it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the task was not to take Srdj when talking about reaching the Srdj-Strincjera-Zarkovica line, what was your task, then? To try to take your units as close as possible to enemy positions at the Srdj fort itself, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The aim was to take the series of forts along the Dubrava ridge. Gruska Glava, Gradci, Strincjera, and to get close to Srdj itself along the ridge but not take the facility itself. And I believe the order was for me to take it, but in my decision I refused to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain this distinction between the ridge of Srdj and the facility at Srdj, the feature. What's the difference between the two and what exactly does it amount to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a huge difference. The facility of Srdj itself is just a small part of the ridge, which comprises the so-called Imperijal Fort. It's a massive fort dating back to Napoleon's time, and then there is an underground tunnel linking the fort to the town of Dubrovnik itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the fort itself, there were Croatian forces, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and when the fort of Srdj falls -- it has a central position in defending Dubrovnik from land. As soon as the fort falls, the whole defence of Dubrovnik collapses, and the units are free to walk down straight into town. There is no other line of approach. The distance between the fort and the Old Town is about 500 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Mr. Jokic, I wasn't asking you about any of that. What I'm asking you about is to explain the distinction between the ridge of Srdj and the fort of Srdj because you are bringing your units there, as you say. They are supposed to reach the Srdj line. How far is it from the actual fort?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ridge from which they could have fired on the fort, but not actually take it, from Strincjera -- between Strincjera and Srdj, there are about 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: He has interrupted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wouldn't have called that an interruption. It's a difficult line to draw between interruption and trying to direct attention to a particular issue. I think Mr. Rodic was doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Yes, that's precisely what I have been trying to do, and I'm doing my best to have my answers as brief and concise as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Jokic, this ridge, is it just a barren ridge?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on that side. It's the lee side, and these are actually positions in front of the Strincjera fort facing Nuncijata and Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I want to know is the following, the distance between that position being reached by your units at the ridge, what is the specific distance between that position and the fort of Srdj itself?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between five and six hundred metres, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Awhile ago you said 300 metres, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen, you want me perhaps to give you specific positions for each of the individual trenches, don't you? No units being brought there, are they? Only weapons are being placed there, and there is a trench at the Strincjera fort so the side of Srdj itself. Weapons are being placed there to prevent weapons from Srdj from strafing across Dubrava and inflicting losses in our units. This is all about the communication between these various forts, Bosanka, Gradci, Strincjera, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please try to be succinct. If I understand you correctly, your unit reached the position at the ridge in order to fire on enemy forces deployed at the Srdj fortress. Those enemy units were disrupting your units, the work of your units on some other positions, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's partially true, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you please tell us the entire answer. Can you please perhaps explain, if that's any easier for you, where your units had been positioned prior to this order for attack. Where were they supposed to be once this order was carried out?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to this attack, the units had been positioned at Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is the distance between Bosanka and Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 700 metres. Six or seven hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at your order for attack, what were they supposed to be doing from this position, given that they were already at Bosanka? What were they supposed to be doing in relation to Srdj? Where were they supposed to go from there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem is that you can't see the overall picture, and I can. I know the context. I'm familiar with that area. I had crossed it a hundred times. From Bosanka you can't see Srdj. You can't target Srdj. What they were supposed to do is pass along the whole series of forts; Gruska Glava, Gradci, Strincjera. This is a wreath of fortresses which you use to reach Srdj from Strincjera, and that's how you gain access to Rijeka Dubrovacka. As for the units at Bosanka, those were not supposed to move towards Srdj. They were not supposed to even budge. It would not have been possible anyway, without taking Srdj, without taking the town of Dubrovnik itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell me, please, how exactly was this supposed to be carried out pursuant to your order? Which lines exactly were they supposed to reach?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My order was carried out precisely as I had planned, these forts that I had talked about were taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please give us the specific lines that pursuant to your order dated the 9th of November your subordinated units were supposed to reach?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you want to refresh your memory, I think we're talking about point 4.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the Dubrava ridge; Gruska Glava, Gradci fort, Strincjera. This is the line. From that line, I would have been able to secure access to Komolac, Tikovici [phoen], and taken control of the various settlements in Rijeka Dubrovacka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a great deal of pressure to take Srdj on the part of the 3rd Battalion also. And that's what the situation was, roughly, that the line was to be taken, including Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get back to that later. But what I'd like to ask you next is the following: Under point 4, what is stated is: "Use the remaining part of the forces to control the territory and to carry out tasks in terms of the logistic support for the units of the 9th VPS and the Military Naval District." What exactly was supposed to be done in relation to units of the Military Naval District?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset, I spoke about this briefly, I believe. My task, in addition to my involvement in the Dubrovnik operation, was to receive the forces of the Military Naval District being evacuated from the Italian border, from the port of Kotor, down through Pula, Rijeka, Zadar, Split, Sibenik and all the way down to Dubrovnik. The entire Military Naval District had hundreds of battalion-level units, platoon-level units, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, we've heard this before, and I'm not going to challenge this. I just wanted you to tell me briefly in this order you wrote, this order for attack, you also make provisions for the logistical support for the units of the 9th Military Naval District being evacuated from Croatia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, plus providing security for the vessels relying on ports within my area. We were providing their supplies also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 5, the tasks of units, specifically here in relation to the 472nd Motorised Brigade, the 1st and the 2nd Battalions in cooperation with the mixed detachment, the 16th Naval Border Detachment and forces of the 9th VPS. From the Bosanka village area on to the village of Ivanica, the attack is to be carried out along the following axis: Bosanka-Mulin Do-Strincjera, and by 1600 hours reach the line Srdj-Strincjera-Gradci. There is an elevation given for Srdj, trig point 403, and in relation to Strincjera K412, and for Gradci K413. Can you please tell us specifically where this elevation 403 was.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srdj is 412, trig point 412, that's Srdj. Maybe on a different map, it would have been given this other number, 403. I'm telling you again the line is defined here, but it does not state anywhere take the actual facility. That's a very important distinction. And furthermore, what we see here is the axis towards Srdj, but it's not actually stated anywhere that the facility itself, Srdj, is to be taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it's not explicitly stated, as you say, and the actual wording is not there, "take Srdj."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the order is to reach the Srdj line by 1600 hours, and then the following elevation and trig point are provided, 403. Is that then the task?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I'm telling you again, this was the task but not to take the actual feature, the actual feature of Srdj. If you insist, in relation to that, I can tell you exactly what steps I took and what explanations I demanded from the order of the 2nd Operational Group in relation to this order to take Srdj itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please just explain the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it might be preferable for that to happen after the break, Mr. Rodic. I think what you're about to put will take --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And may I have the usher's assistance again, please, to hand the witness a document from tab 22. It is the Jokic Prosecution Exhibit P132, tab 30, actually. P132, tab 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, we said under 5.1 that the task of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade was to get out of Bosanka to Biljavaca, and to attack towards Mulin Do-Strincjera, and by 1600 hours to reach the line Srdj-Strincjera-Gradci. Srdj is trig point 403. Can you point this out on the map, this trig point.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Srdj. This trig point 403?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On this map, yes. It's a very small-scale map, and yes, it is 403.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this an inaccurate map?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an accurate map, but I'm saying that on larger scale maps, the place is the same but it is 412, an elevation of 412. But never mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that by 1600 hours, they have to reach the line Srdj trig 403, does that mean that your unit should take that position, get that position?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your order, does it say or does that mean that that unit should get 300 or 500 metres from point 403?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map shows that there is no other feature that could be marked except for Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to answer my question, please. Did you order them to reach the line that was 300 to 500 metres away from point 403?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ordered them, or rather, the chief of staff who was in charge of this operation and Colonel Kovacevic, that they must not take Srdj, if you want a precise answer from me. Ask the command of the 2nd Operational Group why it says "take Srdj." The chief of staff of the 2nd Operational Group, General Damjanovic, signed that order, not only for that day but also for the 11th and the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you said that to the chief of staff Zec and Colonel Kovacevic, who was your assistant for land forces. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your order for the attack on the 9th of November, there is no mention of that? In the written order, that is.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the order, it does not say "take the feature of Srdj." For all of those three days, the fighting went on, but for every one of these days the order was "Do not take the feature of Srdj."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, it is no longer necessary for you to mark anything on the map so would you please focus on the questions now. In your order, it says "Reach Srdj at point 403," in this order dated the 9th of November that we're reading. But if I understand things correctly, apart from what it says here, you said to your chief of staff and your assistant commander for land forces not to take Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me why you did not write that in your written order for the attack?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I have been trying to explain to you, but you won't let me explain. As soon as the order came from the command of the 2nd Operational Group, I asked for an explanation why Srdj is being taken and whose order this is. Is it the order of the command of the 2nd Operational Group or of the chief of General Staff? Since the commander was not at the OKM, General Strugar was not there, and the signator of the 10th of November, there was a decision on action to be taken by the 2nd Operational Group, and it was signed by General Damjanovic. It was his signature that was there. He said to me that this was the order of the command of the 2nd Operational Group but that also in the directive of the General Staff, there is mention of that. I said that we would carry this out, but that we would not take the feature itself. In these operations, I was by the 3rd Light Brigade that was operating in the Sumet/Komolac area. I was with Colonel Bojovic, because this was the first time that that unit was being brought into combat, this 3rd Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said all of that to General Damjanovic, who is deceased now, or rather he has been deceased for a long time now.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, that decision bears the signature of General Damjanovic who was alive then, and his signature is on that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you write anything to the chief of staff of the 2nd Operational Group, Damjanovic, or to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group? Did you object in writing in relation to that? Did you give your reasons why you thought otherwise? Are there any written traces of that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there aren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on, under 5.1, it says that the objective is to break enemy forces in the broader region of Srdj/Dubrava. And when reaching the ordered line, should be fortified at the line of Zarkovica point 315, Srdj point 403, Strincjera point 412, and Gradci trig point 353. And in this way, establish full blockade from Dubrovnik land and Gruz from the southern side of Rijeka Dubrovacka. Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see that section?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, when you say "upon reaching the lines ordered, take inter alia Srdj, point 403," where was that supposed to be? Where were they supposed to fortify themselves there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer because the interpreters did not hear the first part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The witness is not wearing his headphones, so perhaps that is why the -- if we could just go back and repeat the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for your capacity to observe, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: A whole line of questioning appears to have been missed. If we could perhaps repeat that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is only the witness's last answer that we did not hear from the beginning, all the villages mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat the last question. When reaching the lines ordered, it says "To be fortified on the line of Zarkovica, Srdj, Strincjera, Gradci." Can you tell us, in relation to Srdj, point 403 as it says here, where were they supposed to be fortified? Where were your units supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the front part should take the ridge, between the fort of Strincjera towards Srdj, so that they could target Srdj from the flank and Nuncijata on the right. But without taking the actual feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, how far away is this ridge from point 403, Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact number of metres. Is that what you want?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you don't have to speak in terms of a single metre, but say 10 metres or so.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where a position can be established and where there can be proper shelter for artillery pieces to shoot at a given target but be protected at the same time. That is to say, without reaching the fortress. And for them to be able to operate successfully from the flanks by machine-guns and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what distance was this? Where were they supposed to stop, your units? Where were they supposed to stop?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 500 or 600 metres away from the fort itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, why did you not write this in your order for attack?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot write in an order every single thing. My basic intention was to take this line of fortresses that prevented the entry of the 3rd Light Brigade into Rijeka Dubrovacka, to disable fire from Srdj and action from Srdj, but not to take the fort itself. That was the basic tactical concept that I abided by for all the three days of these operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please explain to me whether the units of the 9th VPS sustained any losses. Did they have any soldiers who were killed or wounded due to fire coming from Srdj, due to Croatian forces firing from Srdj, to be precise?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was a constant fire in that period, before that and after that. That was the most heavily fortified position for the defence of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's not elaborate this any further. We've already heard that. Tactically speaking, how did you envisage stopping the action of Croatian forces from Fort Srdj if you came within 500 metres of them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By gunfire. That we can always cover the fort with gunfire so that they cannot operate. That was very possible because our fire was several times stronger than theirs. It was possible to do that from a shelter without getting to the fort itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that why you came within 500 metres of them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the underlying idea. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in terms of their points of departure where the units left from on the 9th of November, were there also some shelters from where action could be taken towards Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from these initial positions, on the 9th November, from those shelters, did you use firearms and artillery pieces in order to shoot at Srdj, and could you reach Srdj in terms of range?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This was not on the 9th. The order was written on the 9th for the 10th. The operations took place on the 10th. There weren't any on the 9th in this attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say the 9th, I'm referring to the date when the order for attack was written.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the attack was taking place --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 10th, and that is what it says in your order.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this could happen from the initial position. It was within range. And now if you want to know what the underlying idea was, why the attack was launched, if that was the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. My question is as follows: Since you could from those initial positions shoot at Srdj from shelters, too, and actually reach it, then why did you move closer, a very little bit only, so that you would get to a distance of 500 metres from the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did not move from Bosanka towards Srdj. We went around. If you look at the map, you can see that this line of forts goes along the ridge. Gradci, Strincjera. So it's that ridge, it's these forts. That's where the Croat forces were that were operating not only towards Bosanka and Zarkovica, but also Dubrovacka, Rijeka. From that ridge, they were preventing the 3rd Light Brigade from getting down to Rijeka. That is the basic tactical idea for this attack. We were not attacking from the Bosanka/Srdj line, but from Strincjera/Srdj, on the flanks. Because the ridge -- I mean, this part where Bosanka is, it is completely bare and open, and no movement was possible there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me when Strincjera was taken.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was taken on the 12th, entirely taken, including the broader area surrounding the fort. On the 11th, Captain Kovacevic reached the fort with certain elements of his unit, but as for taking the entire broader area surrounding the fort, that took place on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at point 5.3 of the order for the mixed TO detachment. We can read here that the task of the mixed detachment was to support the attack by the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade by using a tank company to attack Zarkovica, the village of Bosanka, and Srdj, Dubac, Orsula, the village of Sumet and the village of Komolac; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So does this constitute an attack on Srdj, then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can use a tank company to carry out an operation along that axis, but this is only the axis. This is not about elements of the infantry moving because they cannot operate in this area. The infantry elements moved along the succession of forts past Strincjera and that's where they took up adequate positions. But not from the direction of Bosanka because there you could only use tanks. This was probably not even a company, there were just three or four tanks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then order that tank company to attack along this axis, Zarkovica, Bosanka village, Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by all means. That would have been the only possible axis of attack. Use tanks to fire to make it impossible [as interpreted] for infantry elements of the 3rd Battalion to carry out an attack from the forts of Strincjera, Gradci, and Srdj, and the access to the feature of Srdj itself. That was the idea, for the firing to focus on the feature of Srdj and to make it possible for elements of the infantry to get as close as possible to the ridge, in keeping with the law and to make it impossible for them to fire on us from the fort itself, but it could have taken any number of axis, the attack itself from Srdj then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the tank company? In this order that we can see here, was it firing in a stationary manner from where it was, without ever moving, or was it supposed to simply move along down this axis, Zarkovica, Bosanka village, Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no moving there. There were two tanks that were dug in at Zarkovica this whole time, and two of them were mobile. And probably they were moving about, yes. Quite naturally. I can't be familiar with every single detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, I need to bring to your attention a transcript error which needs to be attended to I think urgently. On page 40, line 23, I believe the witness said "use tanks to fire to make it possible for infantry elements of the 3rd Batallion..." The transcript reads "impossible," and I wonder if that could be cleared up, please. Again, that was page 40, line 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, can you please clarify this for us. The task of the company, of the tank company, was to attack down the axis Zarkovica, Bosanka village, Srdj. What was this supposed to make possible?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This attack by the tanks was supposed to use tank fire on the feature of Srdj, and this was to make it possible for the infantry elements to operate from the flank, from Strincjera, to fire on Srdj and get as close as possible to it. The tanks were there to link up their fire to the fire from Srdj in order to ensure for a successful attack from the right flank for infantry elements. That was the tactical idea behind this particular piece of support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the tank company, then, pursuant to this order? Does it have the task, among other things also, to attack Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I said. To fire on Srdj, to attack Srdj by firing, and thus ensure the link-up between the defending forces and Srdj and make it possible for the infantry elements to attack from the direction of the Strincjera fort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further, LAV PVO 20/3 millimetres and LAV PVO 40/1 millimetres should be maintained at their current positions and provide fire support for the attack of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Trebinje Brigade. Can you please tell us, which weapon exactly are we looking at here and where was it positioned?
