utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two incomplete batteries, 20 and 40 millimetres respectively, that were used for anti-aircraft defence of the entire Zarkovica area and Bosanka. And at the same time, they were part of the mixed detachment as they had no artillery of their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these weapons positioned?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These pieces were at Zarkovica, at the Batutovo fort. I believe that was the name of the fortification. It was in the Zarkovica area. They had their positions in the Zarkovica area, and anti-aircraft defence is what their task was, as well as providing support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of this specific task, were they supposed to fire along these axes, the axis that the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade was moving along?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at point 5.4 now. This is in relation to the 16th Border Naval Detachment with RTOP 403, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the second sentence, it says: "Prevent the movement of enemy forces during the night from Dubrovnik towards Zarkovica, Bosanka, and Srdj. Discover the enemy's combat positions in the area --"

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: North-west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a position?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. North-west of the island of Lokrum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: North-west of Lokrum. The passage near the Belvedere Hotel, the [Realtime transcript read in error "forces"] fortresses in the Old Town, and the coastal area between the old port and Cape Petka, and these are to be destroyed, keeping in mind that the Old Town should not be fired on.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These units of the 9th VPS, were they not supposed already during the previous night, during the 9th and 10th November, to prevent any movements by enemy units along the Dubrovnik axis and once it was ascertained that there were manoeuvres by these units.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt but there is a misleading reading in the transcript. Page 43, lines 13 and 14. It says "forces in the Old Town." That is not to be found in 5.4 paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the word may be "fortresses" rather than "forces."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry; "fortresses."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see there's general agreement by Mr. Rodic and the witness. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no choice but to agree because that's precisely what the document states, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I believe that what it says is "forces within the Old Town" on the transcript, as opposed to "fortresses." If the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's precisely -- that is precisely where we'd got to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we continue, please, Mr. Jokic. These units of the 9th VPS, was their task already during the previous night, between the 9th and 10th of November, to prevent any manoeuvres by enemy forces from Dubrovnik along these axes, as we said a while ago?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Any time of day and night, there were two boats patrolling the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. What about these positions that are marked here, that are referred to in this item, this point of the order? These navy units, where were they supposed to operate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here "firing on possible forces," the reference here is to possible reinforcements that may be brought in along the Zarkovica, Bosanka, Srdj axis. This is a special reference to artillery forces that, from the area of new town, Petka, Lapad, could be sent towards the Old Town. And the only way to discover this is from the sea. If you patrol the lines, the sea lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this also a reference to a position of the enemy forces at one of the forts inside the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Belvedere Hotel, the passage there, it is completely isolated by a concrete wall. It is impossible to target from land, and the fortresses inside the Old Town, yes, as well as Cape Petka, where the weapons were positioned for the support being given to their defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as soon as firing points were discovered, these were to be reported to the forward command post of the 9th Military Naval Sector in order to coordinate the remaining mortar and artillery fire. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would like to tender this document into evidence, and may it please be given a number as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D57.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the usher's assistance, please. I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit P126 from tab 24.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, you've seen this document during the examination-in-chief, haven't you? This is a combat order by the command of the 9th VPS, dated the 10th of November 1991, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 1, we can see the following: "Use the forces of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, extend the attack along the general axis of Bosanka village, Dugi Doci, Strincjera --" again we have the trig point defined here, 412 -- "and by 1700 hours break through to the following line: Bosanka village, Srdj trig point 403, Strincjera trig point 412, Gradci elevation 353." Is this the same axis that we talked about in the previous combat order dated the 9th of November?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just underneath, does it not say that the remaining forces should stay at the lines reached and support the actions of the units taking part in the attack?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me which artillery weapons were supposed to keep supporting this attack by the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, which specific pieces?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what it says here is support by the mobile border naval battery, 130 millimetres, from the 107th coastal artillery battery, as well as the 122 Howitzer and a 130-millimetre gun from TOC as well as a 120-millimetre mortar from TOC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these heavy artillery forces?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one battery and three guns. Certainly, this could be defined as heavy forces. But this is not, for example, an entire division taking part in the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I assume this would have been sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was the task in relation to the 11th of November?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look under point 1.4 where again the order is specified, the order to the artillery. What it says here is "Pursuant to the command -- to an order of the commander of the artillery of the 9th VPS, support the combat activities of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade with the emphasis on artillery hits on the enemy in the Srdj, Strincjera and Gradci sector in accordance with the firing as planned." In the course of the 10th of November when this order was written in relation to the next day, was any firing by these artillery weapons being planned on these positions or in terms of the time and quantity of the firing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Because they were fortresses, fortified facilities, so the firing was planned in advance with all the elements and weapons. And the forts had not been taken at that time, so this was how matters were regulated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you afraid, in view of the strength of the artillery pieces and the axis of attack in the Srdj area, that hits could have been possible to the town of Dubrovnik or the Old Town itself? Were you afraid that that might have happened?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The fire positions of the 130-millimetre battery and the artillery pieces from the TOC were located at Cilipi airport and in the village of Mocici near Cavtat. The axis of attack of that artillery fire went via Srdj, or rather at Srdj, Strincjera, and Gradci. Therefore, it was leading towards Rijeka Dubrovacka, towards the Greben ridge and further on to Dubrovacka Rijeka, whereas the Old Town and the city of Dubrovnik would remain to the left, more than 90 degrees that way. So there was absolutely no possibility of a shell falling into the city of Dubrovnik at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the distance from which these artillery pieces were active in that situation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 8 and 12 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how far it is, what the distance is from the runway at Cilipi airport, which was where the pieces were located, artillery pieces, to Srdj, the target?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's between 10 and 12 kilometres, 12 or 13 kilometres perhaps, as the crow flies. The greatest danger for the Old Town, if I could put it that way --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I just ask you this: What was the nearest distance from Srdj to the first houses in Dubrovnik? On the slopes of Mount Srdj, in the direction of the Old Town? What was the distance from Srdj to the nearest houses?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a very small distance because the houses on the slope, if you go down from the top of Srdj, they lie at two to three hundred metres. You would find the first houses at two to three hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in the direction of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me where the 120-millimetre mortar was located? Where was that positioned? That is mentioned under point 1.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 120-millimetre mortar position that was supposed to give firepower support to the 3rd Battalion, where was that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those three artillery pieces from the TOC were at the Cavtat fire positions, firing positions at Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about this 120-millimetre mortar? Did it open fire from Cavtat?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking about one mortar, whether it went into operation, whether it fired, and at what targets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you because it says here very precisely in great detail in your order. So I'm not construing anything. I'm just asking you on the basis of what I have read here. It says that the mortar lent support -- a 120-millimetre mortar from the TOC, lent support or was supposed to lend support to the forces of the 3rd Battalion along the axis of attack. Is that correct? So I'm interested in knowing where that mortar was positioned.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That mortar did not have that range, an effective range. It's effective range was 6 kilometres. It can target at 10. But for an effective range, the effective range was up to a maximum of 6 kilometres. So it could have targeted the Hotel Belvedere, which was fortified, but it couldn't have targeted Strincjera, for example. And it probably didn't open fire on Strincjera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it able to reach the Old Town at all?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say no if you say that it could have reached a target at a 10-kilometre distance away?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was its -- the furthest it could have reached, the absolute furthest point. With a rifle, your range would be 6 kilometres. But of course, you use rifles to target targets of up to 1.000 metres, whereas a bullet can hit effectively at 6 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, perhaps this person manning the mortar could have extended himself in targeting that. But tell me something else: Where was the artillery of the 3rd Battalion --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour; speculative and comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- of the 472nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the artillery of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade was when the battalion was going into an attack along the prescribed axis?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the axis was prescribed. It was ordered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. As it was ordered. Pursuant to the order.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The firepower of the mortar battalion of the 3rd -- of the battery of the 3rd Battalion were Ivanica-Uskoplje. That was the axis. I think that they were at the Uskoplje at the time, because that's where the positions were designed and were not changed practically throughout the entire operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those the same positions at which the -- on the 6th of December -- at which they were on the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The artillery battalion, was it also supposed to lend support to its battalion in the attack?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That was its basic task. The battery's basic task was to lend support to parts of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did it indeed lend its support pursuant to this combat order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 1.6, which relates to the artillery and mortars of TOC Prevlaka, and it says, "Under the leadership of the chief of the artillery and the commander of the Prevlaka TOC, in coordination with the unit commanders, during the attack provide support to units attacking in the Srdj Dubrava sector and the wider Rijeka sector." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right and clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it says "in coordination with the unit commanders to provide support in the attack," were there direct links and communication between the commanders of individual units taking part in the attack and this artillery?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, there were. Of course they existed, but if you want me to explain how you give support and who maintains links and communication with whom, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what you've just said is sufficient. Now, with the artillery battalion, the artillery of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, and you said that it lent support to its battalion's attack, tell me please whether from those positions at which it was, did it have a range which would reach the town of Dubrovnik and the Old Town in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the firing positions of this area -- of the area of Uskoplje, that particular battery could reach the Old Town area and another kilometre further perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you afraid of this danger, of the danger of firing possibly at the Old Town when you ordered the deployment and use of that unit and the artillery? Weren't you afraid you might hit the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not order the deployment and use of that artillery. I was in command only of my own artillery, and that was the artillery that you enumerated. And from this document, you cannot see the artillery of the 3rd Battalion coming into use because that was regulated by the commander of that particular battalion. But I can explain this if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, according to this order, pursuant to this order, is it true and correct that you ordered an attack of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell me something about the doctrine of the deployment and use of units in the JNA. According to that, would an artillery battalion take part in lending support to its infantry forces within the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so. That is its purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask for the usher's assistance, again, please. Another document to be distributed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, is this a regular combat order of the command of the 9th VPS for the 10th of November 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Combat report. Interpreter's correction: Regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this document compiled at your command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 1, describing the enemy, you report, or it is being reported that on the circular basis of -- the defence has been persistent, great persistence in defending and fired at our positions on Zarkovica, Dubac, Brgat, Ivanica with MB 82 and 120 MM, and with one to two cannons 76 MM ZIS, fired from the region of Bosanka village and the region of -- it says Svet, perhaps that's an error, on to our positions at Zarkovica, Batutovo, and Koratak [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From mortars at Lazaret used to target positions. Now, can you tell me what it says here, "region of Svet." Perhaps that's a typing error. What do you think?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's Sumet, Sumet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the next sentence, does it state that the hotel resorts and walls of the Old Town are still used for mortar positions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that noted during the combat operations? I assume, since it was included in your regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the island of Lokrum, from fire from a 20-millimetre cannon, sniper fire, were the JNA positions at Dubac being fired at?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did have a 20-millimetre cannon in the forest at the top of the hill on the island of Lokrum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can also see that there was strong sniper and machine-gun fire that the enemy resorted to and that they had the Zolja type and Offa [phoen] type weapons, hand-held rocket launchers, basically.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, anti-tank-type guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under point 2, it says that the units of the 9th VPS, along with support from the artillery, as well as vessels from the sea, and first of all the 3rd Battalion of the 472rd Brigade, Motorised Brigade, launched an attack at 7.00 in the morning, 0700 hours, and that by 1800 hours it had reached the line of Kriz, Bosanka village, trig point 326. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it says "Kriz" is that the crossroads above town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not by Srdj fort. This is another Kriz, or cross, near Bosanka. A small settlement. It's the cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what direction did it reach the Kriz or cross position?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean, what direction? It says here "line."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says "broke out on to the line of Kriz."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanka village had been taken control of, and you can see what the line was. Bosanka was taken control of by this date, the 10th of November. Bosanka wasn't taken on that particular day, it was taken control of between the 8th and 9th. But you couldn't draw a line otherwise but drawing it Kriz-Bosanka because that is the only point on the earth, on the ground, that he could have stipulated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Kriz, or cross, in relation to Bosanka?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is to the left of Bosanka. You have Kriz, then you have Bosanka, Gruska Glava, and then trig 326. And then it goes to Gradci, Obod, the ridge, the edge of the ridge, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that it is to the left of Bosanka, is that looking towards town? Towards the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that way. It was closer to town, at any rate. But it was not the Kriz or cross up at the fort itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, we understood that. How far is this cross or Kriz away from Bosanka? What is the distance?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several hundred metres. I can't be preciser than that. It is situated between Zarkovica and Bosanka. That's where it ought to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far did we say Bosanka was away from Srdj? What's the distance between Bosanka and Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Bosanka and Srdj?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, between seven and eight hundred metres. Less than a kilometre anyway, as the crow flies of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Kriz is situated between --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not on that axis. It's a line, curved line. You can see it on the map if you take a map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Have a look at what it says underneath, "PS of the 9th VPS held a blockade at the port of Dubrovnik." What does "PS" mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means naval forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the naval forces of the 9th VPS held a blockade and supported the firepower of the land forces. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know what the axes were there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the previous document, we said that from the sea, if you have artillery pieces which reinforce the first line of defence, and what can be seen from the sea, then those ships were active with those pieces, such as at Cape Petka, the Libertas Hotel, the Belvedere Hotel, the Usek, the passage there, and you can only target that from the sea. Then there was the island of Lokrum. All these were artillery pieces or weapons which prevented the units of the 3rd Battalion from gaining control of the fort and fortresses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any artillery around the Belvedere Hotel itself?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that artillery in a shelter or screened? If you look at the area in which the JNA units are targeting from the land?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct. You couldn't reach them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that why the ships of the 9th VPS had to be deployed and act from the sea, targeting those artillery positions of the Croats at the Belvedere Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's just how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any refugees in the Belvedere Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, no, there weren't, because the Belvedere Hotel was at the front line of defence. That was the Belvedere/Srdj line, Nuncijata line, and no refugees were allowed to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Croatian forces, forces of the Croatian army put up at the Belvedere Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, since this report relates to the 10th of November, and previously we saw your order of the 9th of November for the units and their deployment for the 10th of November, do you happen to remember, compared to the previous day and what happened on the 9th of November and activity going on there, whether there was a step forward made; and if so, what advancement had been made by the units in their attack between the 9th and 10th of November?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No major progress had been made. And you can see from the line given in this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, can you tell me why there was no major progress? Was there strong resistance perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one of the reasons was, of course, strong resistance. And the second reason was this: The firing of the 3rd Battalion, the actions of the 3rd Battalion weren't best expressed with respect to placing the -- the way in which they placed the companies introduced into battle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, along with the 3rd Battalion, was your assistant for the land forces there, Colonel Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He was there throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the chief of staff, captain of the battleship, Zec? Was he at the positions and axes of attack of your units, especially the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He was at Zarkovica himself, which was where they had a vantage point for the commander of the 3rd Battalion, a lookout post. And from there, they were able to maintain constant links and posts, from that observation post, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the chief of staff, Zec, did he happen to inform you that there had been some artillery hits perhaps on to the Old Town in view of the fact that he was at the observation post at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He informed me in the evening when he reported to me and when we were preparing for combat action the following day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what he reported to you about? What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he informed me that there was targeting towards town by the chief of staff, Major Komar. He didn't know exactly -- he couldn't say exactly whether it was the Old Town in actual fact, but he did speak about targeting towards Srdj and towards the town. Now, we didn't know at the time about the hits in the Old Town. But already the next day, you could see on television and in the press and in the protests by the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff that that was what had happened, that there were hits, that there were shells which fell on to the Old Town basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is it correct that in the regular combat report, there was no mention about that, the one that's in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. There is no mention of that. Well, he did not even know that shells had fallen into the Old Town. At least, that's what he reported to me. But he thought that the chief of staff acted independently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come he didn't know then if he was observing from Zarkovica what was going on in town? All of town can be seen from up there at Zarkovica, especially the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You were asking me what he saw?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the position -- the observation post is on Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that observation post can the Old Town of Dubrovnik be seen?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can even Stradun be seen from there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, was Zec at the observation post at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. His duty was to coordinate the action taken by all units, and he was not stationary at one particular point. He went from one unit to another; he changed places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the course of the day, was it possible, because we see here now that, for example, the attack of the 3rd Battalion lasted from 7.00 in the morning until 1800 hours in the evening. So within that time span, could he notice that something had happened, that a shell had fallen into the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he certainly could have, if he looked, certainly he could have seen it. I cannot say what he was looking at. I was telling you what his task was and where he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the exact information he gave you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that the brigade artillery had opened fire beyond orders and that Komar particularly used artillery fire from the area of Vrastica. That's a ridge below Uskoplje. It's a hilly area where the ZIS cannons were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he include that in the regular combat report?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he did not establish what he had opened fire at, what Komar opened fire at, and we discussed that at the command post in Kupari when I came from the position of the 3rd Light Brigade from Rijeka Dubrovacka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Uskoplje, or rather Vrastica, and the artillery of the 472nd Brigade, you mentioned ZIS cannons. Are they 76-millimetre cannons?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did Zec tell you? Where were these cannons operating?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He established that Major Komar, with his radio transmitter, was issuing orders and guiding the gunfire of that artillery. He stopped him from doing that any further, and then he reported to me when I came to the IKL in the evening, to Kupari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the evening of the 10th of November?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The shell of a ZIS cannon, in terms of its line of operation, from those positions of Vrastica, can it hit the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can, if it misses Srdj. If it misses Srdj. And if, objectively speaking and professionally speaking, speaking in expert terms, if fire had been observed and if one did not want to hit the Old Town, there is no way it could have been hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zec establish exactly that a possible hit in the Old Town came from a ZIS cannon at the position of Vrastica, that is to say, a ZIS 76-millimetre gun from Vrastica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't establish anything. He just established that Komar was handling the fire, and he asked him what he was doing and what it was that he was targeting. And he said to him that he was setting the sights of the cannons on Srdj, or rather the antenna, that that is what was being sighted, a pillar like that. Obviously, that was not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you think? If some shells did fall into the Old Town, where could this have come from, bearing in mind all that artillery and the artillery support given to the attacking units during those days?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the possibilities, the firing possibilities and the range of the guns, the cannons, that were in this encirclement at that time, on the 10th, 11th, and 12th, it could have been all the cannons of the 472nd Brigade. It could have been the artillery pieces of the 3rd Battalion; that is to say, its mortars. Less probably tanks. And it could have been the ZIS cannons that we were discussing. But there was also another possibility. From the firing positions of the 1st and 2nd Battalion, notably the 1st Battalion, which was in the Golobov-Kamen area above Rijeka Dubrovacka, because that was also within the range of the Old Town. It should be borne in mind that the entire brigade was around Dubrovnik then, and the units that were taking over from that brigade, they had already arrived, the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, and two battalions as well of the TO Trebinje, which is quite unlikely. The 3rd Light Brigade could not have because it was not within range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it only your artillery that could not manage to engage such a target, to hit that far?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My artillery could have targeted the Old Town if they wanted to do it on purpose, because they were within range. However, when I spoke a short while ago about the risk involved in the operations of my artillery, that is to say, whether there could be any misses in terms of the Old Town, I precluded that possibility because what should be borne in mind is where the firing positions of these artillery pieces are. It's all clear to me now, but I'd have to show it to you on a map, why I exclude this artillery, my artillery, and I do include all the other artillery. Because the cannons of my artillery are facing Rijeka Dubrovacka. To the left is the town of Dubrovnik at a 90-degree angle. And all the cannons from Trebinje are facing the Old Town. And all the cannons of the 3rd Battalion are facing the Old Town. It is such an obvious thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it correct that then the Old Town was within everybody's range?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you cannot say with any degree of certitude from which artillery piece a shell possibly fell into the Old Town? You cannot say that with any degree of certainty?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak with 100 per cent certainty. But when an estimate is made, say, within 80 or 90 per cent, then it can certainly be said which artillery pieces they are. As I said, I cannot say 100 per cent, but those artillery pieces that were operating against Srdj, those artillery pieces could have caused the falling of one shell, one particular hit or, say, 20 or 30 shells. And it is well known which artillery pieces do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did these artillery pieces operate in accordance with your order to attack Srdj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you already that I commanded my own artillery and the commanders of the subordinate units used their own artillery, and they have their own targets which they receive through my combat order. I was not in charge of the entire artillery or is that my obligation. If we were to pursue that logic, then the commander of the 2nd Operational Group gave orders to take Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are not going to proceed according to that logic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Nor are we going to proceed just at this moment, Mr. Rodic. We'll have the second break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, we established before the break that this regular combat report dated the 10th of November does not contain the suspicions of a possible information as to the effect that the Old Town had been hit. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this perhaps included in some other combat report of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period of time, between the 10th and 12th of November, the chief of staff, Zec, and the assistant for land forces, Colonel Kovacevic, were they staying at the command post of the 3rd Battalion and did they organise the coordination of units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they coordinate artillery fire of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not in charge of that. That was not part of their remit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By coordinating the attacks carried out by the units, since if we look at this order we see that the artillery units, too, had certain tasks, were they in a position to be in touch with those units that were at the time providing artillery support?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were at an observation post from where the firing was being controlled. Artillery officers were doing just that, and they were in a position to make sure that the tasks given to the units were carried out. And that includes the tasks of artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would like to tender this document into evidence and be marked as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D58.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. May the witness be shown Exhibit P118 from tab 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have gone through this document during the examination-in-chief. I will ask you in relation to point 1 of this combat order dated the 11th of November, what about the 472nd Motorised Battalion, were they supposed to provide artillery support by using 122-millimetre Howitzers between 8.00 and 8.30 to fire on the Srdj feature, and to use the 120-millimetre mortar to fire on Komolac between 8.00 and 9.00? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure where you're getting this from. Where precisely is this stated?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the combat order.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the point?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Point 1, 472nd Motorised Battalion. This is the second sentence. It says 120-millimetre Howitzers. Can you see that now?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's not the document I have in front of me. 472nd Brigade, without the 3rd Battalion. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have in front of you --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is dated the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one I'm talking about is dated the 11th of November. Do you have that document now?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After preparing the artillery, forces of the 3rd Battalion, together with a Territorial Defence platoon from Niksic, were to continue the attack along the Gruska Glava-Bosanka village axis with the focus on the Gruska Glava-Srdj axis, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 2, in relation to the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, the last sentence, I'm reading in relation to artillery, it says: "120-millimetre mortar, this battalion was supposed to support the attack of the 3rd Battalion of the 472 Motorised Brigade, carrying out strikes, firing on the broader Nuncijata sector, and provide troop reinforcement from Nuncijata towards Srdj." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the 3rd Light Infantry Brigade, the last sentence, it enjoys the artillery support of a 120-millimetre battery belonging to the 472nd Brigade in the Komolac area, 120-millimetre Howitzer from the TOC, and a 120-millimetre mortar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 4, is any artillery firing from the Prevlaka TOC specified using Howitzers and mortars, both 120 millimetres, that were to provide support for the attack of the 3rd Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2 of this document, it reads: "Between 8.30 and 9.00 on the 12th of November, carry out strikes on Srdj using 122-millimetre Howitzer and 120-millimetre mortars." Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 6 of this combat order, it states: "The units are forbidden from using weapons on parts of the Old Town, except in case fire is coming from there that is lethal for the unit."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this not in theory create a possibility for firing on the Old Town in case the unit was under lethal fire?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is only a possibility to neutralise firing coming from a certain weapon that was firing on the unit and, thus, inflicting lethal fire on unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the JNA then is free to use its own weapons against weapons positioned inside the Old Town, or rather, around the Old Town, weapons that are inflicting losses on these same JNA units, that is.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no information, nor did anyone ever tell us that there were weapons from inside the Old Town that were firing. In all the documents that have been made available so far, the only reference was to a 20-millimetre gun that was mounted on a lorry that was from time to time moving about inside the Old Town. As for any other weapons inside the Old Town or any firing by those weapons from inside the Old Town, there was no such thing. However, it was from the direction of the Old Town, from sheltered positions behind the forts, and the ramparts, yes, that's another thing, and that's something we had in our documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me specifically in relation to this lorry with an artillery piece mounted, this lorry that was moving about the Old Town, if it fires at JNA units, in that case, would your unit enjoy the right to return fire, rather to neutralise that weapon as a firing point?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that 20-millimetre weapon was not used to inflict any fatal losses. This was merely a weapon used for carrying out acts of provocation. They would fire a volley, and then they would take shelter again to fire another one. But this sort of weapon, a 20-millimetre weapon, could not have been used to inflict any losses from that kind of distance, let alone fatal losses. Therefore, this weapon could in no way have been neutralised or fired on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a three-barrel gun, in this case, a three times 20-millimetre three-barrel gun?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have this information. We did not know if this was a single-barrel weapon, a double-barrel, or a three-barrel weapon. We did not know for sure what sort of weapon this was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there several such weapons mounted on lorries moving about?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the Grude area, we captured two trucks with weapons mounted when Admiral Djurevic's helicopter had been shot down. But we didn't find anything like that again until we approached the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the sort of weapons that was mounted on those trucks you captured?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was a single-barrel weapon. The other had two or three barrels, but I can't be sure. One was a single-barrel weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this sort of weapon is being used to fire from the Old Town on Zarkovica. Can this fire possibly kill one of your soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It's talking about from Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a hypothetical question. A soldier could also be killed by rifle fire, sniper fire from the Old Town. Of course this is possible. The answer to your question is yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the objection goes to the fact that the witness never said there was firing from the Old Town. And the question poses specifically to Zarkovica. There's nothing in evidence to suggest that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As I understand it, it's put on a hypothetical basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the reports of the 9th VPS, is there ever any reference to enemy fire coming from the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such reports. And we continued to carry out assessments. Our intelligence, information coming from our observation posts, indicated that from sheltered positions behind the ramparts and fortifications, some mortars were positioned, because that's where the fire was coming from. But not from inside the Old Town, as I said before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The walls or ramparts surrounding the Old Town, in your opinion, is it part of the Old Town itself or not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The walls or ramparts are without a doubt part of the Old Town. But I'm talking about from behind the ramparts, from behind the walls of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More specifically, which side?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our information, our intelligence at the beginning, when we reached the Dubrava ridge, was that between the Argentina Hotel and the Excelsior Hotel there was a 120-millimetre mortar positioned and that they had a warehouse there, because from time to time there was a lorry shuttling between Ploce and positions outside the Old Town. That's one piece of intelligence that we had. This has been verified and is considered to be reliable. Another piece of intelligence that we had was that from the west of the Old Town, from the old hospital area, at about two or three hundred metres from there, there were two weapons positioned. And in our assessment, those were 120-millimetre mortars. Also, at the Pile gate, if you approach the town from the west, in the Bogisica park - we checked this and we know this for sure - there were firing positions with mortar positioned there, 80- and 120-millimetre mortars, three pieces altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your order of the 9th of November, the combat order, under point 1, and we've already referred to this sentence, you say: "Enemy, from the towers or turrets of the Old Town nucleus, uses mobile mortars of 80 and 162 millimetres -- 120 millimetres."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I reacted because it's really nonsensical. A mortar cannot be used from a fortress, from a turret. Otherwise, everyone is mobile. So that's why I reacted. But I said that the turrets and towers were used as a screen because it's behind the walls, ramparts, and turrets. So they were positioned behind this shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why under point 1, when you give out information about the enemy, what is the purpose of this piece of information vis-a-vis your own units then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the purpose is to inform the units of the location of the weapons and the fire that can be expected to come from those weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when it says here from the fortress of the Old Town nucleus, what does that imply? What's meant by that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Different people think different things. It depends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've stated my own views. It is impossible to -- for mortars to be fired from a fortress or turret. That is clear to every soldier. I don't know if it's clear to you. The only weapon that you can use from a turret is a rifle, a missile, but not a mortar. It cannot be deployed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not even the light ones, light mortars?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It must have a soft foundation. You can't place it on stone, concrete, or the like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can it have a provisional soft base, foundation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know what you mean. But I don't think it can have anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can a mortar be fired from a truck, for example? That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very difficult, because it is -- it has a recoil which, when a shell is fired, it must have 2 or 3 metres free space in front of it for the trajectory. It can't be fixed. So that's the greatest problem that you encounter with mortars. That's the problem. They have to have a soft basis or foundation upon which to be positioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what does this piece of information, what purpose does serve, then, that these mobile mortars were placed along the turrets or towers of the Old Town? Was this false information on your part? Were you giving out false information to your units and superior command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you say. I had nothing to do with that assertion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's my question to you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I've answered it. I've already told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I assume that the -- you didn't mention mortars up on turrets as a tourist attraction but as a potential danger to your units. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can say what we like now. You can speak about tourist attractions now if you like. But if we're having a serious conversation and dialogue, then I have already stated reasonable arguments, put forward reasonable arguments, professional arguments, sensible arguments which other people will believe. If you don't believe me, now, there were thousands of documents like this. It's not possible to have every word and sentence absolutely exact and correct. And of course, all the reports that were written, do you think they were correct in every aspect? They cannot be 100 per cent correct. 800 Ustashas within the walls of the Old Town? I don't know if you've ever visited the ramparts themselves. Have you? Do you know what they look like? Do you know whether that would be possible? Can you put up 800 people there? So that's another thing we found among one of the documents. I think we mentioned the document yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this information coming from your units, from your intelligence sources, from your command? Is that where that information comes from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is unreliable, incorrect data which has not been checked out, or first-hand information that was never verified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they go down the chain of command to subordinated units. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. You have information coming from the highest level which is not always correct, let alone other levels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me another thing now, please. Now, a truck with a double-barrel gun or with three barrels, what was it doing in the Old Town? You said that was checked out and verified and that it had been seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, that was not said by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I heard otherwise. But I don't mind, I'll repeat the question again, if need be. But I think that the witness did say something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did you say that you had information about the movement of a truck with weapons on it moving around the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that we received information to that effect within the context of your question when you asked whether it could be a source of fire that led to the death of some men, lethal fire, so then I said what this kind of weapon was used for.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the objection went to the number of barrels. The witness never indicated the number of barrels as to Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your question at line 8 and 9 of 73 did specifically mention a double or triple barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really do think the witness mentioned on page 67 and 68 of the transcript, of the LiveNote, the kind of weapons and what calibre they were on the truck. But regardless of that, let's give the witness a chance to say what he knows about that once again, to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that we received information according to which on that truck there was a 20-millimetre weapon, probably the Erlikon that they had because those were the ones that we seized, but I don't know whether it was a single-barrel, double-barrel, or triple-barrel gun. And I said as a soldier what such a weapon could have caused at the distance from which it was fired, and the firepower that it had to jeopardise our units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say that it was a weapon placed on a truck in the Old Town and that it was used for provocation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what way was provocation effected towards the JNA from this weapon on this truck? How was that achieved?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when there's a cease-fire, the weapon fires a volley and masked behind the buildings in town, or sheltered and screened behind the buildings, you don't know where this volley of gunfire came from. But it is firepower as provocation. So you can't actually target anything with that weapon, that wouldn't be possible from the Old Town, and you can't inflict any lethal bullets, lethal fire. And that's what we were discussing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's make ourselves quite clear here. So when they engage in this type of provocation, does that in fact mean that they open fire from the Old Town and that then they hide behind the buildings within the Old Town of Dubrovnik? When I say "Old Town," I mean the Old Town nucleus of Dubrovnik. Does that mean that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right, it does, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, from the Old Town of Dubrovnik, what is the distance, as the crow flies, to Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 2 kilometres, 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By firing from weapons of this kind, of a 20-millimetre calibre weapon, at that distance, can anybody be killed who is at Zarkovica from that position in the Old Town? Could you kill anyone?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I've told you that you can even hit someone with a sniper and kill them, from the Stradun, and kill a man up at Zarkovica. Of course you can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have the usher's assistance again and present P128 exhibit from tab 26 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a combat order dated the 12th of November, and it was intended for the following day, the 13th of November.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 13th of November, there was no combat because a cease-fire came into force, the truce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the 1st Battalion? Take a look at point 1, please. The 1st Battalion, in coordination with parts of the forces of the 3rd Light Infantry Brigade, was it supposed to improve the combat deployment and carry out a blockade of the villages of Prijevo and Bracevo Selo pursuant to the combat order of the 12th of November?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all that's true and correct. That's what it says. However, during the night, an order arrived -- I don't know exactly what it was, but if we look at the next date, the 13th of November, that was when the cease-fire came into force, and the order came from the General Staff in actual fact during the night, so I don't think these tasks and assignments were ever carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well. But it was a combat order nonetheless, regardless of what happened the next day. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this combat order sent to the 2nd Operational Group and the command of the Military Naval District at the forward command post? Was it also sent to them so that they could be informed of its contents?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here. As far as I know, we just sent in a report. So this could be a mistake as well. I can't really say whether it was an omission, an error, or whether it was intentionally compiled in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you just said that the regular combat reports were sent to the commander of the Military Naval District.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a combat order, a combat document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm just saying. I think that that might have been a mistake because I don't think that we sent out combat orders, but I didn't pay attention to that. There was no need for us to send out this type of document. But of course, I couldn't be a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, there is a translation error I want to bring to Your Honours' attention. In the English version, where it says "two," it says 472nd, and instead of having -- well, it should read "the 2nd Operational Group" instead of 204th. It's not Mountain Brigade, after 472nd, it's Motorised Brigade. It seems to have omitted altogether the 2OG and mistaken it for 204th, which is not a relevant unit. It is conceded by the Defence, it was mentioned, of course, that there was the 2OG as well as the KVPO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that for purposes of exactitude, my colleague should indicate the third mistake as well that's in that sentence. And that is that the KVPO is not the tank platoon but it is the command of the Military Naval District.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We seem to have tidied up a lot of translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have the usher's assistance again, please, for the next document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the document that according to which the subordinate unit, the 472nd Motorised Brigade, is sending to the command of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the contents? Or rather, did the subordinate units have the duty of informing you and reporting to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. This was a soldier who was seriously wounded in the Osojnik region, and he died, succumbed to his wounds, at the hospital in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the command of the 9th VPS regularly receive reports of this kind from their subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had records and lists of the dead and wounded, I assume? Kept records?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I tender this document into evidence as a Defence exhibit and it be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is marked D59.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. I'm sorry. Can I have the usher's assistance, please. May the witness be shown the following document, P125 from tab 23.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, under point 1, you can see an order on setting up a joint detachment of the Territorial Defence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further, you can see that the task of this mixed detachment on the 6th of November by 1500 hours to take the area of Vrastica and Cibaca and take over from the 4th Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade. Was this carried out as ordered?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not further stated that in coordination with the special detachment of snipers and the special platoon of the Niksic TO company, they are to improve the combat deployment and break through to the Srdj-Bosanka sector, fortify there, and organise the defence and control of the city of Dubrovnik? Is that what the task was of this mixed detachment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't have a mixed detachment organising the control of the town of Dubrovnik. Observation, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Observation. Would that imply the positions at Srdj and Bosanka where the defence was to be set up?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not stated anywhere explicitly that their task was to take Srdj. Their task was to take up this position and reach the Srdj-Bosanka area, not to take Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it not say that they should fortify at Srdj and organise the defence and control of the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you can see that sentence right there.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says is where they are to fortify, but it doesn't say that they should take the Srdj feature. How in the world could a mixed detachment carry out a task like that, on the 5th of November of all days? This is a Territorial Defence unit. They do not have the capacity for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why is that what is stated in the document, then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm telling you is that it is not stated anywhere that they should take the feature of Srdj itself. It only says that they should reach the area, the sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which sector do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Srdj-Bosanka sector. In fact, they didn't even take Bosanka to begin with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what was the idea about this detachment setting up the control of the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This detachment held Zarkovica, and they observed the town from there, as did the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From those positions in the Srdj area, as you say, where they were supposed to dig themselves in, the mixed detachment, and to organise the defence, were they in a position from there to control the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they could carry out observation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Observation, in your opinion, is it the same as control? These two different terms, do they have the same meaning?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, observation is a concept that means exactly what it says: You're able to observe. Whereas control is something entirely different. You can read it any way you like. You can take it to mean exactly what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We do agree that control and observation are two different terms with different meanings, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 4, if you could have a look, please, the last sentence, the Territorial Defence platoon from Niksic is to be used in combat reconnaissance on the Zarkovica-Bosanka-Srdj axis; readiness: Immediate. Which means that as early as on the 5th of November, they were supposed to go out and carry out that task, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. You're talking about point 4, right? Which page is that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 3, point 4, last sentence. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately. Page 3, but I can't pin it down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3, you can see points 3, 4, and 5, can't you? This --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command of the republican TO staff units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please have a look at the last sentence, point 4.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Niksic TO, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it supposed to carry out this reconnaissance task along the Zarkovica-Bosanka-Srdj axis immediately?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is this what happened?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say. But this combat order is absolutely unusual because tasks are being given here in relation to the 7th of November, what was supposed to be done, and the 10th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, I'm afraid I must interrupt you. This is an OTP exhibit, and this was tendered during their examination-in-chief, an occasion on which you failed to express your surprise when examined by my colleague about this document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I've seen this one before. This document says 1800 hours, the 5th of November. If you look at page 4 -- rather, page 2, it says "The remaining units of the 472nd Brigade by the 10th of November will carry out the following tasks..." Please, the 7th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the sake of brevity, during the examination-in-chief on the 26th of March, this document was given an exhibit number. This is P125. My apologies. P125.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There's no translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is about the engagement of units over the following period. I was not paying attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Much of that exchange was not translated before. I wonder if we could go back. The Admiral did say some points that were significant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must ask you to try and repeat what you said then, Admiral.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was simply not careful enough, and I failed to notice what this document was really about. So I can only offer my apologies in relation to my remarks a moment ago. What we see in this document is the engagement of units of the 9th VPS over the following period of time, which means between the 5th and as late as the 11th, as I have been able to observe, the 11th of November, which covers a period of the next six days.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is not an executive order and it's not a combat order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there was no question about that in the first place. No one asked you about this being or not being a combat order. Please, let's not waste time. I merely asked, in relation to this document, talks about the deployment of units of the 9th VPS over the next period of time, dash, order. No one said anything about a combat order. I'm just asking about what this document is about. And we only have two brief questions left in relation to this document. Under point 9 --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may just be allowed to clarify point 9 of this document, in view of the time remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No time remains, but carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point 9, Mr. Jokic --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- is it true that artillery units were given the task of fortifying the combat deployment on the firing positions and organising communications system and also to carry out orders from the Kupari forward command post and Kumbor command post?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can just look briefly at point 10 now, the same period of time, the remaining units, the remaining part of your units, were they to provide logistical support for the units that were being evacuated from Croatia during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that completes my examination in relation to this document, so...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That will be time then. We will break until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th day of April, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
